objects.description: Represents a single shader parameter parsed from a source line. Stores binding info (buffer index or push constant), type size and offset, parameter name/description, and numeric range with default and step values. Provides constructors to parse a serialized specification string.
Represents a named sampler with a binding slot index for shader resources.
Describes a texture entry in a preset, including the logical name, optional source path, and sampling flags (linear filtering, wrap mode, mipmapping).
Container for metadata about a shader: filesystem paths (source, output, relative) and classification strings (class name, shader name, category).

Aggregates all data for a compiled/parsed shader: source code and bytecode for vertex/fragment stages, metadata/hashes, parameters, preset-specified parameters, comments, and associated SourceShaderInfo. Constructible with an input path and info metadata.
Holds texture asset data tied to a preset/shader build: input path, raw/encoded data string, metadata via SourceShaderInfo, and preset parameters for configuration.
Top-level preset definition bundling multiple shaders and textures, plus parameter overrides and shared metadata. Instantiated with input path and SourceShaderInfo.

Represents a single shader uniform/parameter including buffer index, byte offset/size, value limits, default/current values, step, and description string. Constructible via its explicit constructor; typically stored in ShaderDef::Params.
Lightweight pair specifying an override value for a named parameter. Contains a parameter name and a float value. Not otherwise managed in this header.
Describes a shader sampler/resource by name and binding slot. Typically stored in ShaderDef::Samplers.

Container for a full shader definition, including parameters, samplers, preset parameter key/values, shader sources or bytecode, hashes, and metadata. Provides helpers to add params/samplers, compute buffer sizes, and frees dynamically-allocated bytecode on destruction when Dynamic is true.

A small owner/descriptor class for texture payloads used by the ShaderGC/ShaderGlass pipeline. Holds a name, raw byte data pointer and its length, a flag indicating whether the data memory is dynamically owned by the instance, and a map of preset parameters. The Param method appends key/value preset parameters. The destructor frees Data via free() only when Dynamic is true and Data is non-null. Construction is default; no copy/move semantics are shown in this header (implicitly generated).

Concrete class grouping a collection of ShaderDef and TextureDef objects plus parameter overrides into a named preset. Provides a virtual Build hook, a helper to add a ParamOverride by name/value, and a MakeDynamic utility that marks contained ShaderDefs and TextureDefs as dynamic by setting their Dynamic fields. Ownership: contains vectors of ShaderDef, TextureDef, and ParamOverride by value. Details of ShaderDef, TextureDef, and ParamOverride are defined elsewhere and not in this header.

Lightweight record holding pointers to a precomputed shader hash and binary data plus its length. It does not own the memory it points to; the pointers are const-qualified, implying read-only access and external lifetime management. Construction requires caller-provided pointers and size; no destructor or copy/move specialization is present, so default semantics apply. Unknown specifics of the data format beyond being a byte buffer.

Container and lookup facility for CachedShader entries. Provides an emptiness check, a static function to compute a hash from shader source text, and a lookup that returns a pointer to a matching CachedShader within its internal vector. Ownership: stores CachedShader objects by value in m_cachedShaders, but each CachedShader holds non-owning pointers to external buffers, so ShaderCache does not manage underlying data lifetimes unless done elsewhere. Details of hash algorithm and lookup policy are not present in this header.
Custom exception type indicating file-related errors. Inherits from std::runtime_error and forwards message strings to the base class. Use to signal I/O or file processing failures in this module.

Utility class providing static methods to compile ShaderGlass slangp shaders and presets, load and process shader sources, and parse preset files. No instances are required; all API is static. Interacts with PresetDef, TextureDef, ShaderDef, SourceShaderDef/Param/Sampler, and ShaderCache types declared elsewhere.

functions.name: ltrim
functions.description: Removes leading whitespace and double-quote characters from the given string in place. Uses std::isspace to detect whitespace and stops at the first character that is neither whitespace nor '"'. Intended for preprocessing token/field strings before parsing.
requirements: s must be a valid, modifiable std::string reference.
Leading characters considered whitespace by std::isspace and the '"' character will be stripped; other characters are preserved.
Function mutates its argument; no return value.

functions.name: rtrim
functions.description: Removes trailing whitespace and double-quote characters from the given string in place. Uses std::isspace to detect whitespace and trims from the end backward until a non-whitespace, non-'"' character is found.
requirements: s must be a valid, modifiable std::string reference.
Trailing characters considered whitespace by std::isspace and the '"' character will be stripped; other characters are preserved.
Function mutates its argument; no return value.

functions.name: trim
functions.description: Returns a copy of the input string with both leading and trailing whitespace and double-quote characters removed. Internally calls ltrim and rtrim on the copy.
requirements: Input is passed by value; the original string is not modified.
Trims characters recognized by std::isspace and the '"' character from both ends.

functions.name: ascii
functions.description: Creates and returns a string consisting only of ASCII characters from the input (bytes with values < 128). Any non-ASCII bytes are omitted. Useful for sanitizing text before display or parsing.
requirements: Input may contain arbitrary bytes; bytes with value >= 128 will be dropped.
Return contains only characters whose underlying byte value is < 128.

functions.name: SourceShaderParam::SourceShaderParam
functions.description: Parses a parameter definition string and initializes a SourceShaderParam. It extracts tokens from s using operator>> and std::quoted to populate name (from the third token), desc (from a quoted string, trimmed to ASCII and stripped of surrounding whitespace/quotes), and numeric fields def, min, max, and optional step. Also sets buffer, size, and defaults i to -1 and other fields to zero/empty where applicable.
requirements: s should contain at least three whitespace-separated tokens before a quoted description string (std::quoted) to correctly set name.
s should then contain a quoted description (e.g., "Some description").
After the description, s should contain three floating-point values: def, min, max, and an optional fourth floating-point value: step. If step is absent, it defaults to 0.
If extraction fails for any field, the corresponding member retains its default-initialized value (name/desc may be empty; numeric fields default to 0), as no error checking is performed.
size and buffer are stored verbatim; buffer uses the convention noted in the member comment (-1 push constant, 0 first UBO, etc.), but no validation is performed.

functions.name: SourceShaderSampler::SourceShaderSampler
functions.description: Constructs a SourceShaderSampler with the provided sampler name and binding index. Stores both values as given.
requirements: name is stored as provided; no validation performed.
binding is stored as provided; no range or uniqueness checks are performed.

functions.name: SourcePresetTexture::SourcePresetTexture
functions.description: Constructs a SourcePresetTexture with the given name. Initializes source to an empty string and boolean flags linear, wrap, and mipmap to false.
requirements: name is stored as provided; no validation performed.
Boolean flags default to false; caller must set them explicitly if needed.

functions.name: SourceShaderDef::SourceShaderDef
functions.description: Constructs a SourceShaderDef, storing the input path and shader info. Initializes format to an empty string; other members use their default constructors (empty strings/containers). Intended to represent a shader definition and associated metadata/assets.
requirements: input is stored as provided; no validation of file existence is performed.
info is copied into the object; its fields are not validated here.

functions.name: SourceTextureDef::SourceTextureDef
functions.description: Constructs a SourceTextureDef, storing the input path and shader info. Other members are default-initialized (e.g., data empty, presetParams empty). Represents a texture resource definition used by presets/shaders.
requirements: input is stored as provided; no validation of file existence is performed.
info is copied into the object; its fields are not validated here.

functions.name: SourcePresetDef::SourcePresetDef
functions.description: Constructs a SourcePresetDef, storing the input path and shader info. Initializes containers for shaders, textures, and overrides as empty. Represents a full preset composed of shaders, textures, and parameter overrides.
requirements: input is stored as provided; no validation of file existence is performed.
info is copied into the object; its fields are not validated here.

functions.name: ShaderParam::ShaderParam
functions.signature: ShaderParam::ShaderParam(const char* name, int buffer, int offset, int size, float minValue, float maxValue, float defaultValue, float stepValue = 0.0f, const char* description = "")
functions.description: Constructs a ShaderParam describing a single shader uniform/parameter, including its buffer index, byte offset/size within that buffer, numeric range, default and step values, and a human-readable description. Typical usage: create and store metadata for a parameter that will later be written into a constant/uniform buffer.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string).
description must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string); default is an empty string.
buffer is an integer buffer index; negative values are not validated here but typically should be non-negative and correspond to a valid parameter buffer.
offset and size represent byte offset and byte size; they should be non-negative; size should be greater than 0 to represent a meaningful parameter.
minValue and maxValue define the allowed range; by convention minValue <= maxValue.
defaultValue is the initial/current value; by convention it should lie within [minValue, maxValue].
stepValue is the recommended increment; by convention it should be >= 0.0f.

functions.name: ParamOverride::ParamOverride
functions.description: Constructs a ParamOverride that names a parameter and specifies a value to override its current/default setting. Typically used to apply external or preset-driven values to shader parameters.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string).
value is an unconstrained floating-point override; no range checks are enforced here.

functions.name: ShaderSampler::ShaderSampler
functions.description: Constructs a ShaderSampler describing a named sampler resource and its binding slot/index in the shader pipeline.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string).
binding is the sampler binding index; no validation is performed here but it should correspond to a valid binding for the target API.

functions.name: ShaderDef::ShaderDef
functions.description: Constructs a ShaderDef container holding shader sources/bytecode, parameters, samplers, and metadata. Initializes collections empty, pointers to null, lengths to 0, and Dynamic to false.
requirements: No arguments; creates an empty definition. After construction, fields such as VertexSource/FragmentSource, bytecode pointers, hashes, and Format are null and must be populated by the caller before use if needed.
If the caller later sets Dynamic=true and populates VertexByteCode/FragmentByteCode, those pointers must be allocated with a malloc-compatible allocator to match destructor behavior.

functions.name: ShaderDef::ParamsSize
functions.description: Computes the total byte size required to hold all parameters assigned to the given buffer index by scanning Params and finding the maximal (offset + size). Useful for allocating uniform/constant buffers.
requirements: buffer is the target buffer index; any integer is accepted. If no parameters match (or buffer does not exist), the function returns 0.
Assumes each ShaderParam's offset and size are non-negative byte quantities; negative values would yield undefined or nonsensical results.
Does not perform bounds checking against any external buffer; it only computes based on stored metadata.

functions.name: ShaderDef::AddParam
functions.signature: void ShaderDef::AddParam(const char* name, int buffer, int offset, int size, float minValue, float maxValue, float defaultValue, float stepValue = 0.0f, const char* description = "")
functions.description: Appends a new ShaderParam to this ShaderDef with the specified metadata, range, defaults, and description. A convenience wrapper around Params.emplace_back with the same arguments.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
description must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (empty by default).
buffer should identify a valid parameter buffer index for your pipeline.
offset and size are in bytes; they should be non-negative; size should be > 0 for a meaningful parameter.
By convention minValue <= maxValue; defaultValue should be within [minValue, maxValue]; stepValue should be >= 0.0f.
No duplicate-name or overlap checks are performed; callers are responsible for avoiding conflicting parameters within the same buffer.

functions.name: ShaderDef::AddSampler
functions.signature: void ShaderDef::AddSampler(const char* name, int binding)
functions.description: Appends a new ShaderSampler to this ShaderDef with the given name and binding slot. A convenience wrapper around Samplers.emplace_back.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
binding should be a valid sampler binding for the intended shading API; no validation is performed here.
No duplicate-name or duplicate-binding checks are performed; callers should avoid conflicts.

functions.name: ShaderDef::Param
functions.signature: ShaderDef& ShaderDef::Param(const char* presetKey, const char* presetValue)
functions.description: Adds or updates a preset parameter entry (key/value) in PresetParams and returns *this, enabling chaining. Useful for attaching preset-driven values or configuration that can be applied before runtime.
requirements: presetKey must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string).
presetValue must be a non-null, null-terminated C string (converted to std::string).
Insertion uses std::map::insert; if the key already exists, the value will not be updated (standard insert semantics). Callers needing overwrite semantics should erase or use operator[].

functions.name: ShaderDef::~ShaderDef
functions.description: Destructor for ShaderDef. If Dynamic is true, frees VertexByteCode and FragmentByteCode using free(). Other fields are not deallocated (they are either managed by std containers or raw pointers not owned by this class unless Dynamic is set).
requirements: If Dynamic is true, VertexByteCode and FragmentByteCode must have been allocated with a malloc-compatible allocator; they will be freed with free().
Callers must not free VertexByteCode/FragmentByteCode elsewhere if Dynamic is true to avoid double-free.
If Dynamic is false, the destructor will not free VertexByteCode/FragmentByteCode; ownership remains with the caller.

functions.name: TextureDef::TextureDef
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes a TextureDef with empty/zeroed state: Name empty, Data set to null, DataLength set to 0, Dynamic set to false, and PresetParams empty. Use this to create a texture definition before populating fields and preset parameters.
requirements: No special preconditions; creates a valid, empty TextureDef instance.

functions.name: TextureDef::Param
functions.signature: TextureDef& TextureDef::Param(const char* presetKey, const char* presetValue)
functions.description: Adds a preset parameter key/value pair to PresetParams and returns *this for call chaining. Uses std::map::insert, so an existing key is not overwritten. Intended to conveniently build up preset parameters for a texture definition.
requirements: presetKey must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string convertible to std::string.
presetValue must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string convertible to std::string.
If presetKey already exists in PresetParams, the call will not modify the existing value (std::map::insert semantics).
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; do not call concurrently with other mutating operations on the same TextureDef instance.

functions.name: TextureDef::~TextureDef
functions.description: Destructor. If Dynamic is true and Data is non-null, frees Data using free(). Otherwise, leaves Data untouched. Use Dynamic=true only when Data points to memory obtained from a compatible C allocator and owned by this object.
requirements: If Dynamic is true, Data must either be null or point to memory allocated with malloc/calloc/realloc (or otherwise compatible with free).
If Dynamic is false, the destructor will not free Data; the caller/owner must ensure Data remains valid or is freed elsewhere as appropriate.
Do not set Data to memory obtained via new/new[] when Dynamic is true, as the destructor uses free().
Ensure no other component will free Data when Dynamic is true to avoid double-free.

functions.name: PresetDef::PresetDef
functions.description: Default constructor that initializes an empty preset: ShaderDefs, TextureDefs, and Overrides are empty; Name and Category are empty strings; ImportPath is default-initialized. Intended as the starting point before populating shaders, textures, and parameter overrides.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object can be used immediately after construction; members start in an empty/default state.

functions.name: PresetDef::Build
functions.description: Hook for constructing or configuring the preset’s contents. The base implementation does nothing; derived classes should override to populate ShaderDefs, TextureDefs, and Overrides, and set Name/Category/ImportPath as needed. Typical usage is to call Build() on an instance to prepare it before use.
requirements: May be called on a valid PresetDef (or subclass) instance at any time; no side effects in the base implementation.
Derived overrides should remain noexcept-safety and ordering constraints consistent with callers’ expectations if any exist (not specified here).

functions.name: PresetDef::OverrideParam
functions.signature: void OverrideParam(const char* name, float value)
functions.description: Adds a parameter override to the preset by appending a ParamOverride constructed from the provided name and value to the Overrides list. Use to set or replace shader parameter defaults at runtime/preset-build time.
requirements: name must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C-string that remains valid for the duration of the call.
value may be any float; no range constraints are specified.

functions.name: PresetDef::MakeDynamic
functions.description: Marks all ShaderDef and TextureDef entries in this preset as dynamic by setting their Dynamic field to true. Use after populating ShaderDefs and TextureDefs to indicate they may change at runtime.
requirements: Has effect only on elements currently present in ShaderDefs and TextureDefs; elements added after the call are not automatically marked dynamic unless this is called again.
Requires that ShaderDef and TextureDef elements have a writable boolean member named Dynamic (implied by code).

functions.name: ShaderCache::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the ShaderCache contains no cached shaders. Typical usage is to check whether any cached entries exist before attempting lookups or inserts.
requirements: May be called on any ShaderCache instance at any time; it does not modify state.
No preconditions on object initialization beyond being a valid ShaderCache instance.
Thread-safety is unknown; callers should assume no implicit synchronization.

functions.name: ShaderCache::CalculateHash
functions.description: Computes and returns a hash for the given shader source text as a vector of 32-bit words. Intended to generate a deterministic key for caching. The exact algorithm and output size are not shown here; based on context, it likely matches the hash format used by CachedShader::hash.
requirements: Input parameter 'source' may be any std::string; empty strings are allowed unless higher-level logic forbids them (not specified here).
No exceptions or error codes are documented; callers should handle any standard library exceptions that std::string or std::vector operations might throw.
The length of the returned vector is unspecified here; do not assume a fixed size unless enforced elsewhere (e.g., HASH_LEN).

functions.name: ShaderCache::FindCachedShader
functions.signature: const CachedShader* ShaderCache::FindCachedShader(const std::string& source) const
functions.description: Looks up a cached shader by the provided shader source text and returns a pointer to the corresponding CachedShader if found; otherwise returns nullptr. Intended to be used to avoid recompiling or reprocessing shaders when an identical source has already been cached.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for nullptr before dereferencing.

The returned pointer refers to an element stored inside ShaderCache::m_cachedShaders; its lifetime is tied to the ShaderCache instance and remains valid until the ShaderCache is destroyed or its internal vector is modified in a way that invalidates references (e.g., reallocation).
Input parameter 'source' should be the exact shader source string used for caching; matching behavior depends on the cache’s hash/lookup logic (implementation not shown).
Function is const and does not modify the cache state.

data_types.description: A generic free-form byte string returned by FUZZ_PARAM_STR that may contain any bytes including whitespace, quotes, and non-ASCII characters. It is used as text fields, names, keys, descriptions, or general input strings without a prescribed format.

A string representing a filesystem path returned by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. The value is used to construct std::filesystem::path objects and is expected to reference files on disk; the filename itself is fuzz-generated while the file contents may exist with random data.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting arbitrary strings that are valid for all fuzzer stubs
# expecting FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We focus on covering:
# - Leading/trailing whitespace and quotes (for ltrim/rtrim/trim)
# - Mixed ASCII and non-ASCII (for ascii)
# - Quoted descriptions and numeric-looking tokens (for SourceShaderParam spec builder)
# - C-string suitability (embedded NULs sometimes, but keep many without NUL to be safe)
# - Reasonable filename-like paths used by stubs constructing std::filesystem::path
# The blob returned is a bytes buffer that the harness will split as needed.

MAX_LEN = 4096

ASCII_WS = [" ", "\t", "\r", "\n", "\f", "\v"]
QUOTES = ['"', "'"]

CONTROL_CHARS = [
    "\x00", "\x01", "\x02", "\x03", "\x04", "\x05", "\x06", "\x07", "\x08",
    "\t", "\n", "\x0b", "\x0c", "\r", "\x1b"
]

# A small pool of UTF-8 multi-byte sequences (non-ASCII) to exercise ascii()
NON_ASCII = [
    "é", "ö", "ñ", "€", "💡", "中", "漢", "🚀", "✓", "∞", "∑", "β", "µ", "α"
]

# Filename components and separators to form valid but diverse paths
FILENAME_CHUNKS = [
    "preset", "shader", "texture", "data", "config", "meta", "image", "audio",
    "video", "readme", "notes", "assets", "bin", "src", "include"
]
EXTS = [".txt", ".cfg", ".json", ".yaml", ".glsl", ".hlsl", ".spv", ".bin", ".dat"]
SEPS = ["/", "\\"]
DRIVES = ["C:", "D:", "Z:"]

NUMERIC_STRS = [
    "0", "1", "-1", "3.14", "-273.15", "1e6", "-2.5e-3", "42", "0.0001", "100000"
]

KEYWORDS = [
    "param", "buffer", "offset", "size", "min", "max", "default", "step",
    "name", "desc", "category", "class", "binding", "ubo", "push"
]


def rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n_min: int, n_max: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(n_min, n_max)
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-." + " "+"\t\n\r"
    return "".join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))


def rand_quoted(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a quoted string with possible embedded spaces and quotes escaped
    inner = rand_ascii(r, 0, 40)
    # Insert some non-ASCII occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        inner = insert_non_ascii(r, inner, r.randint(1, 3))
    # Escape internal quotes minimally by backslash to look like C++ quoted
    inner = inner.replace('"', '\\"')
    return f'"{inner}"'


def insert_non_ascii(r: random.Random, base: str, count: int) -> str:
    s = base
    for _ in range(count):
        pos = r.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + r.choice(NON_ASCII) + s[pos:]
    return s


def make_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build paths like: C:\dir\file.ext or /a/b/c.ext
    parts: List[str] = []
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        # Windows drive
        parts.append(r.choice(DRIVES))
    # Start with root or relative
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("")  # leading separator for absolute on POSIX
    depth = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name = r.choice(FILENAME_CHUNKS)
        # sprinkle ascii and digits
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            name += str(r.randint(0, 999))
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            name = insert_non_ascii(r, name, 1)  # sometimes introduce UTF-8 in directory names
        parts.append(name)
    file = r.choice(FILENAME_CHUNKS)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        file += str(r.randint(0, 9999))
    ext = r.choice(EXTS)
    file += ext
    parts.append(file)
    sep = r.choice(SEPS)
    # Join carefully to avoid double separators from drive/root tokens
    path = sep.join(p for p in parts if p is not None)
    return path


def make_shader_param_like_line(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct something that looks like the spec string the fuzz stub composes:
    # three tokens, then a quoted desc, then def min max [step]
    tok = lambda: rand_ascii(r, 1, 8)
    token1 = tok()
    token2 = tok()
    token3 = tok()
    desc = rand_ascii(r, 0, 24)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        desc = insert_non_ascii(r, desc, r.randint(1, 2))
    qdesc = '"' + desc.replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
    defv = r.choice(NUMERIC_STRS)
    minv = r.choice(["-100", "-1", "0", "-3.5", "-10.0"]) if r.random() < 0.5 else str(round(r.uniform(-1000, 0), 3))
    maxv = r.choice(["1", "10", "100", "3.5", "1000"]) if r.random() < 0.5 else str(round(r.uniform(0.001, 2000), 3))
    parts = [token1, token2, token3, qdesc, defv, minv, maxv]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        step = str(round(abs(r.uniform(0, 10)), 4))
        parts.append(step)
    return " ".join(parts)


def make_leading_ws_quote(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Leading whitespace/quotes to exercise ltrim
    lead = "".join(r.choice(ASCII_WS + ['"']) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
    core = rand_ascii(r, 1, 40)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        core = insert_non_ascii(r, core, 1)
    return lead + core


def make_trailing_ws_quote(r: random.Random) -> str:
    core = rand_ascii(r, 1, 40)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        core = insert_non_ascii(r, core, 1)
    trail = "".join(r.choice(ASCII_WS + ['"']) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
    return core + trail


def make_ascii_only(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return rand_ascii(r, 0, 64)


def make_with_controls(r: random.Random) -> str:
    s = rand_ascii(r, 0, 40)
    # insert a few control characters including a single NUL sometimes
    count = r.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(count):
        ch = r.choice(CONTROL_CHARS)
        pos = r.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + ch + s[pos:]
    return s


def make_kv_pair(r: random.Random) -> str:
    key = r.choice(KEYWORDS) + ("_" + rand_ascii(r, 2, 6) if r.random() < 0.7 else "")
    val = rand_ascii(r, 0, 20)
    return f"{key}={val}"


def assemble_corpus(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build multiple lines separated by newlines; FUZZ_PARAM_STR often pulls substrings
    pieces: List[str] = []
    # Ensure presence of each category at least once
    pieces.append(make_leading_ws_quote(r))
    pieces.append(make_trailing_ws_quote(r))
    pieces.append(rand_quoted(r))
    pieces.append(make_ascii_only(r))
    pieces.append(make_with_controls(r))
    pieces.append(make_shader_param_like_line(r))
    pieces.append(make_kv_pair(r))
    # Add several filenames
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        pieces.append(make_filename(r))
    # Add extra random lines to diversify
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            pieces.append(make_leading_ws_quote(r))
        elif choice < 0.30:
            pieces.append(make_trailing_ws_quote(r))
        elif choice < 0.45:
            pieces.append(rand_quoted(r))
        elif choice < 0.60:
            pieces.append(make_shader_param_like_line(r))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            pieces.append(make_with_controls(r))
        else:
            pieces.append(make_ascii_only(r))
    blob = "\n".join(pieces)
    b = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > MAX_LEN:
        b = b[:MAX_LEN]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_corpus(r)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single blob that the harness splits to feed
# FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (filesystem paths) and FUZZ_PARAM_STR (plain strings).
# We focus on generating plausible filesystem paths (with directories, extensions,
# relative/absolute forms, and characters commonly seen in shader tooling) and
# reasonable ASCII strings for class/shader/category names.
# Size is capped under 4096 bytes.

SEP = "\n"  # delimiter between entries
MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# A selection of useful file extensions seen in shader/preset pipelines
FILE_EXTS = [
    ".slangp", ".glsl", ".hlsl", ".fx", ".spv", ".bin", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml",
    ".txt", ".inc", ".h", ".hpp", ".metal", ".wgsl"
]

# Directory and base-name tokens to create varied paths
DIR_TOKENS = [
    "shaders", "src", "data", "assets", "presets", "textures", "materials",
    "include", "common", "effects", "passes", "cache"
]
BASE_TOKENS = [
    "basic", "phong", "pbr", "toon", "water", "glass", "bloom", "ssao",
    "motion_blur", "tonemap", "gamma", "noise", "voronoi", "fbm", "checker",
    "compose", "mix", "color", "lut", "shadow", "depth", "sky", "clouds"
]

# Additional filename decorations
DECOR_TOKENS = ["vs", "fs", "vert", "frag", "comp", "lib", "include", "part", "stage"]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, allow_spaces=False) -> str:
    # Generate a component with letters/digits and occasional dashes/underscores
    length = rng.randint(3, 16)
    chars = SAFE_ASCII + (" " if allow_spaces and rng.random() < 0.2 else "")
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length)).strip()
    # Ensure not empty and not just dots
    if not s or set(s) == {'.'}:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, BASE_TOKENS)
    return s

def _rand_rel_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a relative path like: ./shaders/pbr/fs.glsl or presets/water.slangp
    parts = []
    # Occasionally start with ./ or ../
    prefix = rng.choice(["", "./", "../"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else ""
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        part = _rand_choice(rng, DIR_TOKENS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_component(rng)
        parts.append(part)
    # base name
    base = _rand_choice(rng, BASE_TOKENS)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += "_" + _rand_choice(rng, DECOR_TOKENS)
    # optional numeric suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base += f"_{rng.randint(1, 9)}"
    ext = _rand_choice(rng, FILE_EXTS)
    filename = base + ext
    path = "/".join(parts + [filename]) if parts else filename
    return prefix + path

def _rand_abs_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate an absolute path for POSIX style; sometimes include spaces
    depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
    parts = []
    for i in range(depth):
        if i == depth - 1 and rng.random() < 0.9:
            # filename
            base = _rand_choice(rng, BASE_TOKENS)
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                base += "_" + _rand_choice(rng, DECOR_TOKENS)
            if rng.random() < 0.35:
                base += f"_{rng.randint(10, 999)}"
            comp = base + _rand_choice(rng, FILE_EXTS)
        else:
            comp = _rand_choice(rng, DIR_TOKENS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_component(rng, allow_spaces=True)
        parts.append(comp)
    path = "/".join(parts)
    return "/" + path

def _rand_windows_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a Windows-like path with drive letter
    drive = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
    parts = []
    for i in range(depth):
        if i == depth - 1 and rng.random() < 0.9:
            base = _rand_choice(rng, BASE_TOKENS)
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                base += "_" + _rand_choice(rng, DECOR_TOKENS)
            comp = base + _rand_choice(rng, FILE_EXTS)
        else:
            comp = _rand_choice(rng, DIR_TOKENS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_component(rng, allow_spaces=True)
        # replace forward slashes if any
        comp = comp.replace('/', '_')
        parts.append(comp)
    return f"{drive}:\\" + "\\".join(parts)

def _rand_fs_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of relative, POSIX absolute, and Windows paths
    ptype = rng.random()
    if ptype < 0.5:
        return _rand_rel_path(rng)
    elif ptype < 0.8:
        return _rand_abs_path(rng)
    else:
        return _rand_windows_path(rng)

def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=24) -> str:
    # Class/shader/category names: allow dots and slashes occasionally to exercise parsing
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    # Occasionally add namespace-like structure
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, ["Core", "FX", "Post", "Render", "Material"]) + "::" + s
    # Occasionally add category-style path
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, ["utility", "stylized", "lighting", "post", "experimental"]) + "/" + s
    return s

def _make_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    entries: List[str] = []
    # For each fuzzer stub, we need 4 filenames + 3 strings (info) + 1 filename (input)
    # The three stubs are similar; to improve coverage, generate a set of 3 blocks
    blocks = 3
    for _ in range(blocks):
        # SourceShaderInfo paths
        entries.append(_rand_fs_path(rng))  # sourcePath
        entries.append(_rand_fs_path(rng))  # outputPath
        entries.append(_rand_fs_path(rng))  # relativePath
        # className, shaderName, category
        entries.append(_rand_identifier(rng))
        entries.append(_rand_identifier(rng))
        entries.append(_rand_identifier(rng))
        # input path
        entries.append(_rand_fs_path(rng))
    return entries

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = _make_entries(rng)

    # Ensure reasonable total size; if oversized, trim entries conservatively from the end
    blob = (SEP.join(entries)).encode('utf-8')
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Trim by removing some trailing entries
        while entries and len(SEP.join(entries).encode('utf-8')) > MAX_TOTAL:
            entries.pop()
        blob = (SEP.join(entries)).encode('utf-8')

    return blob
